Subject: PO setup and billing cadence questions for Redwood pilot

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Procurement at MediGrid is ready to onboard the pilot but we need to confirm a few procurement constraints before we can issue a PO:

- Our AP team requires a single Purchase Order per legal entity (we operate 3 entities in the US).
- Requested payment terms: Net60 (standard for our enterprise) — any chance of matching?
- We prefer consolidated monthly invoices, but for the first month we want a pre-billing invoice (to cover setup credits/fees).

Can you confirm Redwood’s PO header requirements and whether Net60 / pre-billing can be accommodated? Also please send your PO template so I can validate with AP.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Senior Procurement Specialist
MediGrid Systems
procurement@medigrid.com

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO setup and billing cadence questions for Redwood pilot

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: we can accept POs per legal entity, we can do consolidated monthly invoices, and we can support a one-off pre-bill for month zero as a commercial exception. Net60 is not our standard on self-serve hosted accounts, but it can be evaluated for pilots tied to a committed spend — happy to propose an approach.

Detail / asks:
- PO headers: we need (1) MediGrid legal name + entity ID, (2) PO number, (3) billing address, (4) remit-to = Redwood Inference, EIN, and Redwood billing contact. I am attaching our PO template for AP (Medigrid_PO_Template.pdf).
- Net terms: typical is Net30; for Net60 we’d ask for a 10% up-front pre-bill for the first invoice or an advance credit to mitigate DSO. If you can commit to a minimum monthly seat/usage threshold for the pilot (we can propose tiers), we can move to Net45 with a staged rollback to Net60 after 3 months and a clean payment history.
- Discounts / packaging: discounts are volume and commitment based. If MediGrid can sign a 6-month pilot with an expected token cap, I’ll route a 12% pilot discount to finance for approval.

Looping in Ben on finance specifics. If this works, I can send a redlined SOW and a DocuSign envelope for signatures.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
(Attachment: Medigrid_PO_Template.pdf)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <procurement@medigrid.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: PO setup and billing cadence questions for Redwood pilot

Alicia — appreciate the detail. Finance can accommodate a commercial path with these guardrails:

- Proposed terms: Net45 standard for pilots with a one-time pre-bill equal to 25% of the estimated first-month consumption. After three on-time invoices, we can re-evaluate full Net60.
- Invoice cadence: monthly consolidated invoice by default. We’ll allow separate PO numbers per entity but prefer one consolidated invoice that lists PO numbers per line.
- Attachment: I’m attaching the Redwood Master SOW (Redwood_Master_SOW_v3.pdf) for scope/commitment language. Please confirm expected monthly commitment so we can lock discount bands.

If MediGrid signs to a 6-month pilot with minimum monthly commitment of $45k we can apply a 12% pilot discount and Net45 terms as above. If commitment is below that, discount drops to 7% and pre-bill remains at 50%.

Next steps: Alicia, can you confirm the expected first-month usage estimate and the legal entity names so I can produce an invoice preview? Once we align, Priyom will handle the PO language and DocuSign.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
(Attachment: Redwood_Master_SOW_v3.pdf)
